summary: Watauga County lookout on Dugger Mountain: 35-ft steel tower in 1929, 60-ft tower in 1941, a part-time fire spotter in 1980; no source after 1983 on its condition.

facts.status_note: A 1983 survey description records the tower. I found no later source on whether it still stands.

staffing.status: staffed part-time in spring and fall

facts.agency: North Carolina Division of Forest Resources

events.note: A 35-foot steel tower erected near Penley, per the state biennial report quoted on the Forest Lookouts page.
A 60-foot tower erected by the CCC and the North Carolina Forest Service. The page does not say whether it replaced the 1929 tower.
Clemmie Watson had spent 36 years in the tower each spring and fall and worked part-time for the N.C. Forest Service.
NGS station description: four legs, silver, about 75 feet tall.

corrections.why: 10.7 m is the height of the 1929 35-foot tower. The same page records a 60-foot tower in 1941 and an NGS description of about 75 feet in 1983.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Sources give 35 feet (1929), 60 feet (1941) and about 75 feet (1983 NGS description). The story gives each figure with its date. The 1983 figure is the latest recorded height.

sources.title: This week in the archives: Fire tower lookout, breeding winners, neighborhood planning overlay

notes_for_editor: The brief height of 10.7 m is the 1929 tower, not the current one. The Forest Lookouts page quotes the 1928 newspaper and the 1929 and 1941 state reports secondhand; originals were not checked. The 1980 Watauga Democrat piece is the only staffing record. No source after the 1983 NGS description says whether the tower stands or how the site is reached, so the status is unknown and access is left out. The firetower.org photo dugger-mountain.jpg is already in photos_manifest.json, so no new photo is listed.
